title: A Day on Venus Is Longer Than Its Year, and It's True
description:
Venus spins once on its axis in 243 Earth days but circles the Sun in 225. Find out why the Sun rises in the west there and how long a Venus day really lasts from sunrise to sunrise.
#space #venus #astronomy #shorts

scenes.narration: A day on Venus outlasts its whole year. Seriously.
scenes.imagePrompt: planet venus glowing pale yellow in deep space, thick swirling clouds, soft sunlight from one side, ultra detailed, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Venus takes two hundred forty-three Earth days to spin once on its axis. That's the slowest spin of any planet.
scenes.imagePrompt: slowly rotating planet with motion trails around its axis, black space, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: But it circles the Sun in just two hundred twenty-five days. The year ends before a single spin does.
scenes.imagePrompt: the sun with a small bright planet on a curved orbital path, glowing orbit line, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Venus also spins backwards. So the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.
scenes.imagePrompt: alien sunrise over a rocky horizon under a thick hazy orange sky, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Here's the twist: thanks to that backward spin, sunrise to sunrise takes about one hundred seventeen Earth days.
scenes.imagePrompt: giant hourglass standing on a volcanic plain, dim yellow light, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Not that you'd actually see the Sun. The sky is hidden behind thick clouds of sulfuric acid droplets.
scenes.imagePrompt: dense layered yellow clouds seen from inside an alien atmosphere, oppressive haze, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: And at the surface it's over four hundred sixty degrees Celsius. Hotter than Mercury, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
scenes.imagePrompt: scorching volcanic surface with glowing cracks under a heavy orange sky, deep midnight blue palette with cyan highlights, cinematic lighting, shallow depth of field, no text

scenes.narration: Could you survive one day on Venus? Tell me in the comments.
